evals.prompt: Draft a bug report. On build 184, exporting an invoice with tax details omits zero-value lines. The accepted invoice specification says every line must be present. It reproduces in Chrome and Firefox. We suspect the CSV serializer but have not confirmed that.
evals.expected_output: A tracker-ready defect report with authoritative expected behavior, observed behavior, reproduction context, impact or unknown impact, verification conditions, and the serializer theory labeled as a hypothesis.
assertions: The item is classified as a defect report rather than a feature request or implementation task.
Expected and actual behavior are stated separately and the expectation cites the supplied specification.
Build and browser evidence are preserved without invented environment details or impact.
The serializer cause remains explicitly unconfirmed and the brief reflects the discrepancy.

evals.prompt: Write a feature request from this customer note: 'Add a CSV button.' The customer needs account owners to reconcile invoice history in an external accounting system. This is one request; we have no usage study or delivery commitment.
evals.expected_output: A feature request centered on the reconciliation need and desired outcome, with the CSV button retained only as a possible solution and evidence accurately limited to one request.
assertions: The title and summary describe the affected party, limitation, and desired outcome rather than only the button.
CSV is visibly optional unless the supplied need makes that format mandatory.
Demand is not generalized beyond the single customer note.
The item does not imply accepted requirements, priority, design, or implementation authorization.

evals.prompt: Update the live incident record. Checkout has returned to normal in Europe after traffic was shifted at 14:32 UTC, but the root cause is still unknown. The incident lead is Sam. Preserve the earlier 14:10 hypothesis that the database pool was exhausted even though later metrics did not support it.
evals.expected_output: An updated incident record with current restored impact and response state first, timestamped mitigation and evidence, explicit ownership, and a retained but corrected hypothesis chronology.
assertions: The title and summary are re-derived for the current incident state.
14:32 UTC mitigation and restoration evidence are distinguished from unknown root cause.
The 14:10 hypothesis remains in the timeline and is not rewritten as fact or deleted.
Permanent correction and post-incident work remain separate follow-up artifacts.

evals.prompt: Rewrite only the title and summary of this issue. Its body says mobile users cannot complete checkout when a saved address contains a newline. Do not change scope, priority, owner, acceptance criteria, or status.
evals.expected_output: A concise, discriminating title and one- or two-sentence summary derived only from the existing body, with every other field unchanged.
assertions: The title identifies the affected behavior, result, and material condition.
The summary says what is wrong and why it matters without adding unsupported facts.
No scope, priority, owner, acceptance criterion, status, or proposed fix is introduced.
The response makes clear that only the brief changed.

evals.prompt: Turn this untriaged feature request into file-by-file implementation tasks so engineering can start today. The request says teams want faster audit exports but has no accepted behavior, threshold, or design.
evals.expected_output: A boundary response that preserves the feature request as intake and declines to create implementation tasks from missing accepted behavior and design.
assertions: The item remains a feature request rather than being silently advanced to delivery work.
Missing accepted behavior, performance threshold, and design are named.
No file-by-file tasks, estimates, priority, or implementation authorization are produced.
The response identifies the next decision or workflow needed without inventing it.

evals.prompt: Draft one defect report and capture all supplied context. An artifact preview receives a 422 application/problem+json response, but the CLI replaces it with a generic error and exit code 1. Investigation confirmed that the generated HTTP client throws before its response reaches the command. Accepted design: a transport adapter extracts status and body from the foreign failure and decodes it once into ServiceProblem; the command adapter preserves the status and chooses the exit code. Illustrative interface sketch: ServiceFailure = { status: number; problem: ServiceProblem }. Accepted sequence: add the extraction helper, fix preview and publish adapters, then audit the remaining service endpoints. Testing strategy: unit cases for valid and malformed problem bodies, adapter contract tests for status and fields, CLI output snapshots, and an end-to-end service response. Behavioral verification: the CLI exposes the service status plus problem type, title, and detail. Open question: whether invalid non-problem JSON should be logged.
evals.expected_output: A tracker-ready defect report that retains the complete confirmed investigation, accepted adapter design, illustrative interface sketch, accepted implementation sequence, layered testing strategy, behavioral verification conditions, and unresolved logging question without confusing any of their authority states.
assertions: The item remains a defect report and states the 422-to-generic-error discrepancy and confirmed foreign-client boundary.
The accepted transport and command adapter responsibilities, illustrative interface sketch, and three-step sequence are all preserved rather than compressed into a generic proposed fix.
The four testing layers remain distinct from the behavioral verification conditions.
The logging question remains unresolved, and no supplied design detail is treated as authorization to implement or create child tasks.

evals.prompt: Write a defect report. In version 3.4, saving a profile with a two-character family name clears the display name. The accepted profile contract requires the display name to remain unchanged. It reproduces every time. We have no root cause, design, implementation plan, or testing strategy yet.
evals.expected_output: A focused defect report with expected and actual behavior, reproduction and version evidence, honest unknown impact, and behavioral verification conditions, without fabricated technical design or empty planning sections.
assertions: The accepted expectation, actual result, version, and deterministic reproduction are preserved.
No root cause, architecture, code sketch, implementation sequence, testing strategy, tradeoff, or decision is invented.
The report does not add empty technical-context headings merely because the guide permits them.
Behavioral verification conditions cover the original failing case without prescribing a mechanism.

evals.prompt: Draft a defect report from the supplied evidence. The investigation and behavioral verification conditions are accepted. A cross-cutting error-translation design affecting six commands is still proposed and is authoritative at docs/design/error-translation.md. Option A duplicates decoding in commands and is simpler locally but can drift; option B centralizes decoding in adapters and is recommended for consistency, but no decision has been made. Keep only the design status synopsis and link in the issue.
evals.expected_output: A defect report that preserves accepted investigation and verification evidence while summarizing and linking the proposed cross-cutting design, both options, their tradeoffs, the recommendation, and the still-open decision.
assertions: The item keeps the accepted investigation and behavioral verification conditions separate from the proposed design.
The issue contains a concise design-status synopsis and the authoritative document link rather than a divergent copy.
Both options and tradeoffs are retained, option B remains a recommendation, and no accepted decision is claimed.
The presence of a detailed external design does not silently create implementation tasks or delivery approval.

evals.prompt: Draft the accepted delivery issue for this approved change and preserve every supplied detail. Replace generic `flow:point kind=policy` comments inside the existing managed Policies region with a contained `flow:policy source=<versioned-id>` marker. The enclosing region remains format v1 and is still the only ownership unit; the contained marker has no local version and extends to the next policy marker or region end. Accepted TypeScript sketch: `const MARKER_KIND_POLICY = "flow:policy" as const` and `type PolicyMarker = { readonly kind: typeof MARKER_KIND_POLICY; readonly source: string }`. Accepted parser flow: validate and extract the Policies region first, then recover contributors only from its body; a valid policy marker outside the region is ignored. Remove `MARKER_KIND_POINT`, `pointKind`, generic point parsing, and all current point fixtures. Do not add compatibility reads, migration, a generic contribution abstraction, or paired per-policy fences. Implementation surfaces: the shared marker codec and exports, policy rendering and observation, unit/property tests, graph-projection tests, CLI fixtures, generated help, architecture docs, and managed consumer projections. Behavioral verification: one versionless policy marker per active contribution, unchanged deterministic ordering and aggregate replacement, and no current point syntax. Testing strategy: codec round trips including IDs containing `@` and `/`, missing-source failure, outside-region observation, direct and bundle-contributed policies, CLI lifecycle coverage, and producer/consumer convergence. Open question: whether a supplied marker-local `v` should be rejected or ignored.
evals.expected_output: A tracker-ready accepted delivery item that preserves the complete ownership and containment design, exact TypeScript sketch, parser flow, removals, non-goals, implementation surfaces, behavioral verification conditions, layered testing strategy, and unresolved marker-local-version question without reclassifying the accepted work as intake or inventing further design.
assertions: The item remains accepted delivery work under the host workflow rather than being rewritten as a feature request, defect, or unapproved proposal.
The unchanged v1 ownership region, versionless contained marker, implicit extent, exact TypeScript sketch, and region-first parser flow are all preserved rather than compressed into generic prose.
Every named removal, non-goal, implementation surface, behavioral verification condition, and testing layer remains present and distinct.
The marker-local-version question remains unresolved, and no compatibility path, generic abstraction, paired fence, priority, estimate, or additional implementation decision is invented.

evals.prompt: Draft a tracker-ready defect report from these observed and expected behaviors without inventing severity or root cause.
assertions: The selected skill is author-software-work-items.
No neighboring skill is selected for a job it does not own.
Routing uses only catalog names and descriptions.
No task side effect occurs before selection.

evals.prompt: Three days after a Sentry investigation and root-cause research, prepare the exact Linear defect issue body for creation. The derived research summary is at docs/research-summary.md. Before synthesis, reopen the authoritative current Sentry family at evidence/sentry-family.json rather than relying only on that summary. Preserve the accepted diagnosis and correction, keep the source safe, and state what the tracker readback must verify after creation.
evals.expected_output: A Linear-ready defect report that carries the accepted root-cause research while retaining the initiating Sentry short ID and controlled-access URL from the refreshed authoritative family, followed by a post-write readback check against that source inventory.
assertions: The issue includes the Sentry short ID CHECKOUT-WEB-482 and its exact controlled-access URL.
The current Sentry family supplies provenance instead of the derived research summary being treated as the authoritative source.
The supplied observation time, project, and production environment are preserved without invented counts or event content.
The final verification requires Linear readback to retain the Sentry identifier and link.

evals.prompt: Draft one defect report from the two material monitoring occurrences in evidence/occurrences.json. They support the same diagnosed billing defect. Keep the report concise, but make each initiating occurrence independently recoverable.
evals.expected_output: One defect report whose source inventory preserves both monitoring occurrences as separate identifier-and-link entries with their supplied observation times and shared project and environment.
assertions: BILLING-201 appears with https://monitor.example.test/issues/BILLING-201 and 2026-08-20T11:03:00Z, and BILLING-233 appears with https://monitor.example.test/issues/BILLING-233 and 2026-08-22T18:41:00Z.
The two occurrences are not collapsed into an untraceable count or one representative link.
The shared billing-api project and production environment remain associated with both occurrences.
No event IDs, raw logs, request bodies, or unrelated source fields are invented.

evals.prompt: Write a defect report from an AlertWatch notification that checkout failed in production. The authoritative occurrence was deleted before handoff, so its stable identifier, URL, and observation time cannot be recovered. assertions: AlertWatch is retained as the source system and production as the known environment.
The stable identifier, URL, and observation time are explicitly marked unavailable.
No identifier, timestamp, count, project, correlation value, or link is invented.
The report remains actionable about the observed checkout failure without disguising the provenance gap.

evals.prompt: Draft a defect report from manual QA. On build 211 in the staging environment, a tester observed that saving an empty optional nickname clears the account display name. The accepted profile contract says the display name must remain unchanged. No tracker or source link was supplied.
evals.expected_output: An ordinary manual-QA defect report with the supplied build, staging environment, expected and actual behavior, and honest absence of a source link, without irrelevant Sentry or monitoring fields.
assertions: Manual QA is identified as the discovery activity and the supplied build and staging environment are preserved.
Expected and actual behavior remain separate and cite the supplied profile contract.

No Sentry identifier, Sentry URL, monitoring event ID, explicit monitoring classification, or monitoring-specific placeholder is added. A generic occurrence count or an honest generic source-unavailable note is not a monitoring field.

The summary is concise and intentionally omits the Sentry pointer. Preserve the authoritative pointer without copying raw event content.
